title: `reduce_window` with a window of size 1 and negative padding aborts the process in XLA

found: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875 fixed it, imported as https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51962 (merged 2026-11-04).

description: If every window dimension and stride of `lax.reduce_window` is 1 and negative padding shrinks the operand,
compilation fails a `CHECK` in XLA, which aborts the Python process with `SIGABRT` instead of raising.
The crash happens for `add`, `max` and generic computations, with and without `jit`,
and on either axis of a 2-d operand.
A window of size 2, a padding that keeps the size, and the variadic form with several operands all work.
expected: `lax.reduce_window` accepts negative padding, which removes entries, as `lax.pad` does,
and the StableHLO verifier accepts it too.
A window of size 1 should then return the padded operand,
e.g. `[2.]` for `[1., 2.]` with padding `(-1, 0)`, as `lax.pad` computes.
reproducer: # With a window of size 2, padding (-1, 1) works.
# A window of size 1 with padding (-1, 0) kills the process, so it runs in a subprocess.
cause: In XLA. JAX emits a `stablehlo.reduce_window` with `padding = [[-1, 0]]`,
which the StableHLO verifier accepts and the StableHLO reference interpreter evaluates to `[2.]`.
`AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleReduceWindow` replaces a reduce window with a trivial window
by an elementwise `add` of the operand's shape, ignoring the negative padding, and `ReplaceInstruction` fails:
fix: In XLA. Until then, JAX can lower such a reduce window as a `pad` (a slice) followed by the elementwise operation.
lean: `reduce_window` is not modelled. `scripts/shapes.py` does not test it.
